notes:
LAMOST-HVS5 through LAMOST-HVS14: these ten are the paper's newly identified, retained unbound candidates (T:p5-b6; T:p14-b1; T:p15-b0; T:p15-b1); their LAMOST designations are linked to the HVS names in I:p14-b1, I:p15-b0, and I:p15-b1. LAMOST-HVS14 is retained despite the later caution that its velocity variation could be binary-related (T:p11-b2).
LAMOST-HVS1 through LAMOST-HVS4: follow_up stars, because the paper states LAMOST had previously identified four B-type unbound HVSs (T:p1-b7) and names this range among the earlier discoveries (T:p2-b3). HVS1, HVS3, and HVS4 are recovered in the new sample, while HVS2 is manually added because it is not in the official release (T:p4-b1; T:p5-b3).
HIP 60350: follow_up, recovered as a previously known hyper-runaway/HVS (T:p4-b1; T:p13-b8) and described as unbound in this paper (T:p13-b4).
SDSS J081828.07+570922.1: follow_up even though the paper now calls it the 'bound HVS' (T:p4-b1); it was previously discovered by Brown et al. and is counted among the known HVSs in the final sample (T:p13-b8).
No Gaia source IDs are given in the supplied text or tables, so none are recorded. Other high-velocity objects are not included because the paper does not retain an explicit present-day Milky Way unbound classification for them; only the ten new objects are newly classified as unbound (T:p5-b6).

LAMOST-HVS1: LAMOST-HVS1 is mentioned as a previously known HVS recovered in the sample (T:p4-b1) and discussed qualitatively in T:p13-b4. It also appears in Figures 2 and 9 (I:p6-b0, I:p17-b1), but the supplied text and tables do not give explicit numerical position, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, total velocity, or bound/unbound probability for LAMOST-HVS1. Table 2 notes that its complete version is available online (T:p10-b0), but the relevant row is omitted from the supplied excerpt; values are therefore not extracted from plotted positions.

LAMOST-HVS2: LAMOST-HVS2 was manually added to the final sample (T:p5-b3) but was not recovered in the DR10 search because it was discovered from LAMOST test data (T:p4-b1). The supplied Table 2 excerpt (T:p10-b0 / I:p10-b0) does not include its row, and the supplied text contains no numerical right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, total Galactic-rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability for LAMOST-HVS2. It is only discussed qualitatively (e.g., T:p13-b4: “LAMOST-HVS1 and HVS2 face flight time issues when traced back to the GC”) and appears as a labeled point in Figures 2, 6, 8, and 9 without printed values. Therefore no quantity values for LAMOST-HVS2 are extracted.

LAMOST-HVS3: The supplied Table 2 is truncated and does not include the LAMOST-HVS3 row, so exact astrometric, distance, proper-motion, and radial-velocity values for LAMOST-HVS3 are not provided in the supplied text. The two retained values are approximate readings from the plotted point in Figure 2 (I:p6-b0), not exact tabulated measurements. Text at T:p13-b4 discusses LAMOST-HVS3's orbit/origin but gives no numeric quantities.

LAMOST-HVS4: LAMOST-HVS4 is identified as a known LAMOST HVS at T:p4-b1 and appears in Figure 2 (I:p6-b0), but the supplied excerpt of Table 2 (T:p10-b0 / I:p10-b0) does not include its row. Thus no explicit tabulated coordinates, parallax, proper motion, heliocentric distance, radial velocity, or bound/unbound probability are available in the supplied material. The two plotted quantities above are approximate readings from Figure 2; no numerical uncertainties are reported for them in the supplied text. T:p10-b4 states that LAMOST-HVS4 has the largest v_rf in the sample but does not give its numerical value.

LAMOST-HVS5: Table 3 (I:p14-b1/T:p14-b1) also lists v_rf = -157.1 ± 7.0 km/s for LAMOST-HVS5; this is a Galactic-rest-frame radial velocity and is not recorded as radial_velocity because that quantity is restricted to heliocentric or barycentric line-of-sight velocities. The narrative (T:p5-b9) gives v_los = -207.48 ± 6.99 km/s, consistent with the adopted Table 3 value v_los = -207.5 ± 7.0 km/s.

LAMOST-HVS6: Target LAMOST-HVS6 (LAMOST J171230.82+110924.5). Table 3 gives both v_los = -318.6 ± 2.7 km/s and v_rf = -187.2 ± 2.6 km/s; only the heliocentric v_los is recorded as radial_velocity, since v_rf is measured relative to the Galactic rest frame. The star is classified as an "unbound HVS candidate" qualitatively (based on comparison with the escape-velocity curve), but no numerical bound/unbound probability is reported. Table 3's G-band absolute magnitude (M_G = 2.44 ± 0.60) is not one of the requested quantities.

LAMOST-HVS7: For LAMOST-HVS7 (J110108.23+360918.0), Table 3 reports v_rf = -424.4 ± 6.6 km/s (T:p14-b1); this is a Galactocentric rest-frame radial velocity, not a heliocentric/barycentric radial velocity, so it is not extracted as radial_velocity under the rules. The text's adopted mean radial velocity of -417.13 ± 6.65 km/s (T:p8-b1) corresponds to the Table 3 value -417.1 ± 6.7 km/s, which is recorded once with the table precision. No parallax or bound/unbound probabilities are reported for this star.

LAMOST-HVS8: For LAMOST-HVS8, Table 3 (T:p14-b1; I:p14-b1) also gives v_rf = 313.7 ± 1.2 km s−1, the Galactic-rest-frame radial velocity; it was not recorded as radial_velocity because the required quantity excludes velocities relative to the Galactic standard of rest. The paper labels LAMOST-HVS8 an unbound HVS candidate (T:p5-b6, T:p8-b3) but reports no numerical parallax or bound/unbound probability.

LAMOST-HVS9: For LAMOST-HVS9 (J125538.89+352338.8), Table 4 reports v_rf = 319.7 ± 3.4 km/s, a Galactic-rest-frame radial component; it is not treated as the heliocentric radial_velocity. No parallax or numerical bound/unbound probabilities are reported for this star.

LAMOST-HVS10: For LAMOST-HVS10, the paper reports both heliocentric v_los and Galactocentric-rest-frame v_rf (T:p15-b0; T:p10-b1). I retain v_los as radial_velocity and exclude v_rf because the rules exclude velocities relative to the local/Galactic standard or rest frame. The three individual LAMOST RVs are reported as separate measurements, and the adopted average is also recorded. No numeric parallax or bound/unbound probability is reported for this star.

LAMOST-HVS11: The paper identifies LAMOST-HVS11 as an unbound HVS candidate but does not report a bound or unbound probability. Its Galactic-rest-frame radial velocity v_rf = 369.5 ± 1.4 km/s (T:p15-b0) is not used for radial_velocity because the requested quantity is the heliocentric or barycentric line-of-sight velocity.

LAMOST-HVS12: LAMOST-HVS12 is described as a new unbound HVS candidate (e.g. T:p10-b4 and T:p13-b9), but no numerical bound or unbound probability is reported, so no probability quantity is submitted. The paper also reports v_rf = 488.3 ± 3.9 km/s in the Galactic rest frame (T:p15-b0); this is not used as radial_velocity because the rules exclude velocities relative to the Galactic standard of rest. The submitted radial velocity is the heliocentric v_los. The distance and Galactocentric radius are not based on a directly reported parallax for this star.

LAMOST-HVS13: For LAMOST-HVS13, the text at T:p11-b1 reports two velocity/distance solutions depending on the assumed absolute magnitude: 690 ± 162 km/s and Galactocentric distance 13.0 kpc for B9V, and 797 ± 192 km/s and 14.6 kpc after adopting the B9III magnitude. Table 5 gives the adopted values as 796.7 ± 191.7 km/s and 14.63 ± 3.04 kpc. Table 5 also prints M_G = 0.515 ± 0.525 with the footnote “From the best-fitted B9III star HD175640,” while the text identifies 0.515 ± 0.525 as the B9V value and 0.205 ± 0.525 as the B9III HD175640 value; this appears to be an internal inconsistency in the table/footnote, but the adopted radius and total velocity match the text’s B9III solution. The table’s v_rf = -177.5 ± 9.4 km/s is a Galactocentric rest-frame radial velocity and is not extracted as radial_velocity. No parallax or bound/unbound probabilities are reported for this star.

LAMOST-HVS14: Target is LAMOST-HVS14 (J015022.75+483631.1). The paper reports two discrepant LAMOST epochs and adopts the higher-SNR solution in Table 5; the lower-SNR alternative is retained above as a separately reported result. The paper describes LAMOST-HVS14 as a new unbound HVS candidate by comparing its total velocity with the escape velocity, but it does not report a numerical bound or unbound probability, so no probability quantity is entered. The paper's v_rf values are Galactic-rest-frame radial velocities rather than heliocentric/barycentric line-of-sight velocities; they are not entered under radial_velocity. Relevant passages: T:p11-b2 and T:p15-b1.

SDSS J081828.07+570922.1: The supplied Table 2 excerpt does not include the row for SDSS J081828.07+570922.1. The paper identifies it only as a recovered known bound HVS and shows it as a labeled black square in Figure 2. I therefore report the position encoded by the SDSS designation and approximate plotted values for its Galactocentric distance and total velocity; no exact tabulated values are provided in the supplied material.

HIP 60350: HIP 60350 is identified in the supplied text only as a previously known hyper-runaway star recovered in the sample (T:p4-b1, T:p13-b4), and it is plotted in Figure 2 (I:p6-b0), Figure 8/its caption (T:p16-b0), and Figure 9 (I:p17-b0, I:p17-b1). The supplied Table 2 is truncated to a few example rows and does not include HIP 60350; its complete online version, which might contain numerical astrometry/velocities/distance, is not provided. No explicit numerical position, parallax, distance, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, total Galactic-rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability for HIP 60350 is reported in the supplied material, so no quantities are extracted.
